content:
Apple has reached a $250 million class-action settlement over delays to Siri and Apple Intelligence, and it's now moving through the court system. Here's how the $250 million will be paid out, who's eligible, and more.

Apple $250 million Siri settlement

Apple was hit with a class-action lawsuit last year over its repeated delays to some of the Siri and Apple Intelligence features it first unveiled at WWDC 2024. The lawsuit alleged that Apple promoted and advertised AI features that didn't exist and wouldn't exist for years.

The lawsuit claimed Apple generated "unprecedented anticipation" around its Apple Intelligence marketing to "convince consumers to upgrade their devices at premium prices."

Apple agreed to settle the lawsuit in December, with terms unveiled in May. As part of the settlement, Apple did not admit any wrongdoing. At the time, Apple told 9to5Mac it was settling to "stay focused on what we do best — delivering innovative products and services for our users."

In its statement, Apple also promoted its already-launched Apple Intelligence features, including Writing Tools, Clean Up, and Visual Intelligence.

As spotted by MacRumors, Apple's settlement received preliminary approval from a judge last week following a hearing on July 8. This means the case can now proceed to the next phase. The judge rejected arguments that the settlement lumped together class members with wildly varying claim amounts.

Who qualifies

The biggest news for iPhone users is that Apple will be paying out a portion of the $250 million to affected iPhone owners.

The eligible class includes people who purchased an iPhone model with Apple Intelligence capabilities between June 10, 2024 — when Apple announced the features — and March 29, 2025 — shortly after Apple announced the delays.

Here are the relevant device models:

  • iPhone 15 Pro
  • iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16e
  • iPhone 16
  • iPhone 16 Plus
  • iPhone 16 Pro
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max

How much will Apple pay iPhone users?

Apple's settlement is $250 million, but a large chunk of that will go to attorney fees and other legal costs first. For iPhone users themselves, it's expected that each eligible device will receive around $25.

However, that amount isn't set in stone and depends on how many claims are ultimately filed. If more eligible users file claims, the payout per person could be lower. If fewer people claim, each eligible device could receive up to $95.

How to file a claim

For now, eligible iPhone users don't need to do anything. The case has now received preliminary approval and can move forward. As part of the process, a notification inviting claims will be issued within 45 days of last week's approval — meaning no later than August 31, 2026.

When filing a claim, you'll need to provide proof of purchase for an eligible device, such as a serial number. You'll also need to provide your Apple Account information and phone number.

Verita Global, the settlement administrator for the case, will set up a website for users to file their claim information. However, the site isn't live yet. We'll be sure to let everyone know once it's available.

That said, it'll still be a while before payouts go out. The final approval hearing for the payments — not just approval of the settlement terms — won't happen until September 29, 2027, and checks won't go out until at least 60 days after that.

Wrap-up

Are you eligible for a piece of Apple's $250 million settlement over Siri and Apple Intelligence delays? Do you think this settlement is fair? Let us know in the comments.
